title: The Calcutta Quran Petition
byline: by Chandmal Chopra and Sita Ram Goel · Voice of India · 1986, third edition 1999
lede: In March 1985 Chandmal Chopra, a Calcutta citizen, filed a writ petition in the Calcutta High Court. He argued that since Indian law punishes writing that promotes enmity between communities or insults a religion (sections 153A and 295A), and since Muslims had used those laws against critics of Islam, the same test should apply to the Quran. The petition set off protests across South Asia, and the High Court dismissed it within weeks. The book reprints the case papers and adds Goel's long commentary on jihad.
facts: petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution
Justice Bimal Chandra Basak dismisses it
when Bangladesh police fired on protesters at Chapai Nawabganj on 11 May 1985, as reported at the time
note: The petition sought to have a scripture declared unlawful, which courts and governments rejected as an attack on religious freedom. This page records what happened and what each side argued, from the documents in the book. It does not endorse the petition.
